title: The readout's chemistry, the readout's reliability, and the consequence for a leaderboard
cost: $0. Offline. CPU only, OMP_NUM_THREADS=8. No API call, no GPU, no network.
why_this_exists: A review of R1 raised four objections that, if they stand, remove the paper's headline rather
than qualify it. Three of them are answerable from data already on disk and are answered here.
The fourth (venue fit) is answerable by an experiment this paper's own thesis implies and has
never run. Everything else the review raised is a matter of wording and is not an experiment.
W4 (chemistry). R = 1 - rho_ij / sqrt(rho_i^2 + rho_j^2). The objection is that mutating a G-C
pair and mutating an A-U pair change base composition differently, so the probing readout's
baseline could differ by pair type for reasons that have nothing to do with whether the pair
forms. The objection has a sharp structure the review did not state: the COMPENSATORY DOUBLE
mutant preserves base composition exactly (G-C -> C-G, A-U -> U-A), so the numerator rho_ij
carries no composition change at all. Every composition change in R lives in the denominator.
That makes the denominator the whole test.
W3 (reliability). The paper reports a reproducibility ceiling for the DESIGN SCORE and none for
R, and every causal claim in the paper is about R. The corpus releases per-nucleotide
reactivity errors; R's own noise is therefore computable and has never been computed.
W9 (consequence). The paper asserts that a placement channel matters for how design models are
evaluated and never measures it. The corpus has a method label and a wet-lab benchmark score
for every design. Whether the leaderboard moves when placement is held fixed is a one-run
question and it is the paper's own claim turned into a measurement.
W5/W2 (internal consistency). The paper withdraws every mediated fraction its pipeline produced
and then prints one as a headline. Prop. 4 gives an estimator-free bound that the depth channel
has never been put through. Separately, Def. 3's prose says every program in the corpus
optimises a nearest-neighbour objective; the corpus has nine methods and most are neural.

arms.V: Reproduce the published matched rescue contrast +0.05393 and the published dG contrast -1.72454 from the same builders. Nothing below is read if V fails.

A_chemistry.A0: Report the corpus's experiment_type census. A base-specific reagent and a base-agnostic reagent do not license the same objection.
A_chemistry.A1: The matched G-C minus A-U contrast, same strata as the headline (design x min(depth,3) x crossed), with the outcome replaced by D = sqrt(rho_i^2 + rho_j^2), the single-mutant disruption baseline. Puzzle-clustered interval.
A_chemistry.A2: The same with the outcome replaced by rho_ij, the compensatory-mutant disruption.
A_chemistry.A3: The headline contrast on R, re-run with a caliper on log D added to the stratification (quintiles of log D within the existing cells). Retention against the unconditioned +0.05393.
A_chemistry.A4: A2 minus A1 read as a decomposition: how much of the R contrast is the numerator moving and how much is the denominator moving.

B_reliability.B1: Parametric bootstrap of R through the released per-nucleotide reactivity_error columns, 200 draws per record, giving a per-pair SD(R). Report the median and the quartiles, and express the headline +0.05393 in units of that SD and in units of the between-pair SD of R.
B_reliability.B2: Census of the denominator: quantiles of D, and the headline contrast re-run after dropping the bottom decile of D.
B_reliability.B3: Split-half reliability of the contrast itself: 200 random halves of the target clusters, correlation of the two halves' matched contrasts.

C_leaderboard.C1: Rank the nine design methods by their mean benchmark score. Re-rank after post-stratifying every method's designs onto one common placement distribution (bins of the design's G-C-minus-A-U depth gap). Report Kendall tau between the two rankings and the largest rank movement.
C_leaderboard.C2: The share of the between-method score spread that survives the reweighting.

D_consistency.D1: The depth channel through Prop. 4: bin-wise h on depth, its oscillation, d_TV between the two exposure arms, the crude bound and the tight bound, against the printed product-route reading 71.2%.
D_consistency.D2: A target-clustered bootstrap interval on the tight bound of the primary channel, 400 resamples, at the binning the paper reports.
D_consistency.D3: The dG null re-run on two subsets of methods: the ones that consume a thermodynamic objective (Eterna, Rosetta) and the neural ones (MPNN-fixbb, MPNN-RFdiff, gRNAde, gRNAde-no3d, Shujun_struct2seq, Shujun_shape_struct2seq).

staked_predictions.claim: The disruption baseline D differs between the two pair types: A1's 95% interval excludes zero.
The rescue contrast survives conditioning on the disruption baseline at no worse than 60% of its unconditioned value, with an interval excluding zero.
Dropping the bottom decile of the denominator retains at least 70% of the contrast.
Holding placement fixed moves the leaderboard: Kendall tau < 1.0 and at least one method changes rank.
The depth channel's tight Prop.-4 bound is below 100% of the total contrast, so the channel is bounded rather than vacuous.
The dG null holds on both method subsets: neither subset's retention leaves the placebo band reported in Section 5.3.

kill_conditions.K0_verification_failed: V does not reproduce the published contrasts. Nothing below is read.
kill_conditions.K1_readout_is_chemistry: A3's retention falls below 0.40 or its interval covers zero. Then the headline rescue contrast is not separated from the disruption baseline, and Section 5.2's claim must be re-scoped to a statement about the released column rather than about pair formation.
kill_conditions.K2_outcome_too_noisy: B2's retention falls below 0.40, or B3's split-half correlation is below 0.10. Then the outcome cannot carry the decomposition and Sections 6.1-6.2 must say so.
kill_conditions.K3_no_leaderboard_consequence: C1 returns Kendall tau = 1.0 with no rank movement. Then the paper's evaluation claim is null on this corpus and Section 6.3 must be written as a null, not as an implication.
kill_conditions.K4_depth_channel_vacuous: D1's tight bound exceeds 100%. Then the depth channel is in the same position as the crude bound on the energy channel and the 71.2% must be withdrawn rather than qualified.
kill_conditions.K5_null_is_method_dependent: D3 shows the dG null on one subset and not the other. Then Section 5.3's conclusion is a statement about a subset of the corpus and must be labelled as one.

what_this_experiment_may_NOT_do: It may not decide whether a G-C pair is more likely to form than an A-U pair in general. It is
one corpus, one reagent, one released column.
It may not turn a leaderboard movement into a claim about which design method is better. C1
measures whether the ranking is sensitive to a covariate the designers chose, not which ranking
It may not rehabilitate any withdrawn mediated fraction. D1 and D2 bound; they do not estimate.
It may not be read as a chemistry experiment. A1 and A3 test whether the composition change in
the single mutants can account for the contrast; they do not measure reagent selectivity, and no
It may not extend to a second corpus. Nothing here is run outside the OK7a M2R release except
The stakes above are graded once, in this wording. If the implementation is found defective the
defect is recorded in m61_declaration_erratum.json and this file is not edited.
